messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: auth verification error rate spike detected in prod (rule: auth.verify.error_rate > 5% for 3m). First seen 10:17 UTC. Paging oncall @ashley :rotating_light:
ashley: I'm on it. Can someone post a quick impact summary (console vs API)?
trent: looking at logs now. token-verify service is returning 502/504 when calling https://auth-jwks.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json - spike started at 10:15 UTC. 10:22 UTC: 401s on console auth up ~35% vs baseline. API traffic shows increased reject rate for bearer token verification (internal microservices returning 503).
maria: adding context — yesterday we rolled cloudfront behavior change for jwks caching. Could be propagation/edge misconfig or a bad origin health check.
ashley: good call. Trent, can you paste the recent 5xx/4xx log snippet and any curl result from the jwks endpoint?
trent: paste logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:16:21Z token-verify auth_jwks_fetch error status=502 host=auth-jwks.example.com attempts=1
2026-03-15T10:17:03Z token-verify auth_jwks_fetch error status=504 host=auth-jwks.example.com attempts=2
2026-03-15T10:18:44Z token-verify result=token_reject reason=jwks_unavailable trace_id=tr_abc123
```
curl from a bastion: ```curl -i https://auth-jwks.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json --max-time 5``` -> returns 504 after 5s, retry sometimes 200 with stale payload (old kid set).
ops-bot: Runbook: auth-jwks-outage -> https://redwood.runbooks/jwks-outage (steps: switch to local jwks cache, force-refresh origin, switch CDN origin to backup).
maria: we have a secondary origin (internal s3 bucket) with the last known jwks. Recommend switching cloudfront origin to s3 and clearing the edge cache TTL to 0 for jwks path. That should restore token verification for clients that don't strictly require latest key rotation.
ashley: do it. Trent, coordinate with infra to flip origin. Kevin, stand by to monitor consumer token failures.
kevin: watching dashboards. Preparing customer impact blurb for support. Looks like ~12% of active console sessions failing to login in us-west-2. Mobile clients mostly unaffected (using cached tokens).
trent: initiating origin switch now (cloudfront invalidation staged). Command we ran: 
```
aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id ABCDEF --paths "/.well-known/jwks.json" 
```
deploy-bot: cloudfront origin update job queued: job-id cf-update-2062. Will post status.
ashley: status?
deploy-bot: cf-update-2062: origin switched to s3-origin-ww-standby, invalidation created, propagation in progress (~45s).
trent: quick check: after origin switch, curl returns 200 with JWKS payload (kid list includes last rotated keys). Token-verifier processes now returning 200 for jwks fetch.
ashley: rolling small canary for token-verify (restart pods) to pick up new cache immediately. Using kubectl rollout restart deployment/token-verify -n prod-canary.
maria: note — this is a graceful mitigation only. Root cause still unknown (origin failing or cloudfront health-check flare). Recommend we keep s3 origin for 30m and monitor key rotation timing.
kevin: customer comms draft: "We experienced authentication failures affecting web console logins between 10:15-10:45 UTC due to a third-party JWKS propagation issue. We implemented a failover to a standby origin which restored service for most customers. If you still see login issues, please clear your browser cache or contact support." Thoughts?
ashley: good. Mark as partial mitigation. I'll escalate to infra + CDN vendor and sec to investigate rotation/timing and health-check flakiness.
trent: metrics: 10:15-10:22 UTC peak 401 spike 38%. After mitigation 10:25-10:40 UTC dropped back to 2-3% baseline. Token-verify error rate metric dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/token-verify/errors (shared).
ops-bot: Incident state updated -> partial-mitigated. Action items assigned: infra (investigate origin health & CF health checks), sec (verify no key compromise; check key ids and rotation), devex (baked runbook update for future rapid origin fallback).
maria: small follow-up — we should consider longer TTLs for JWKS or an active local cache that serves last-known keys for short windows to avoid TOT outages during CDN flaps. Also maybe add a fallback to our baked S3 origin in the service code path before bubbling errors upstream.
ashley: agreed. Postmortem required. I'll keep this thread open until root cause confirmed. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
kevin: filing support incident and emailing affected customers now. Will attach timeline and mitigation steps.
ashley: tagging sec and infra for on-call handoff at 11:00 UTC. Oncall shift trent -> infra-lead. Please follow up here with deep-dive findings.
trent: noted. I’ll capture trace samples and origin health logs and upload to the incident folder.
ops-bot: Reminder: please annotate all commits and commands in the incident channel for audit.
ashley: closing pager for now; reopening if error rate rises above 5% again. We will run a scheduled RCA meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
kevin: thanks all.
trent: uploading logs to /shared/incidents/2062001234/logs and will post summary in the RCA.
ops-bot: Incident marked resolved->monitoring."
